meta.name: Create FastAPI application and links router

context.prd-excerpt:
Link Shelf is a local, single-user link store. From the PRD overview: "One endpoint to save a link, one to get them all back, and tags so the list stays navigable past a few dozen entries." No authentication, no multi-tenancy, no sharing.
Three endpoints are planned across this layer, all on the same router this task creates: POST /links (L3-003, feature save-link) GET /links (L3-004, features list-links and tag-links) POST /links/{link_id}/tags (L3-006, feature tag-links)
There is no /api prefix. The analysis pass records the basis: "No /api prefix - the PRD never mentions one."
context.tech-stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI 0.110+ (which brings Pydantic v2 and starlette), SQLAlchemy 2.x, SQLite (file-backed, no server process), pytest 8.x, httpx (required by starlette's TestClient). Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime.
context.template-base: none - analysis.template.path is null. No tree is copied from anywhere.

dependencies.interface:
Provided by L0-004. A virtual environment with the project installed, in which:
python -c "import fastapi, sqlalchemy, httpx"
succeeds, and `pytest` is on PATH. httpx is what makes `from fastapi.testclient import TestClient` importable; it is already declared in pyproject.toml by L0-003 and must not be added again.

Provided by L0-002. An empty package:

This task adds app/api/links.py inside it. Leave app/api/__init__.py empty - main.py imports the module by path (`from app.api import links`), so no re-export is needed.

task.objective: Create the FastAPI application object in app/main.py and an empty APIRouter in app/api/links.py, wire the router into the app, and prove with a smoke test that the application imports and serves. This establishes the two module paths - `app.main:app` and `app.api.links:router` - that every remaining backend task writes against.

requirements.requirement:
Create file `app/api/links.py` containing exactly one module-level name, `router`:
from fastapi import APIRouter
router = APIRouter(tags=["links"])
Pass `tags=["links"]` so the generated OpenAPI groups these routes.
Pass NO `prefix` argument. Every later handler declares its full path instead (`@router.post("/links")`, `@router.get("/links")`, `@router.post("/links/{link_id}/tags")`). A prefix of "/links" would force L3-003 and L3-004 to register the empty path `@router.post("")`, which is easy to get wrong and reads as a bug. L3-003, L3-004 and L3-006 are all written against the no-prefix contract exported below; changing it here breaks all three.
Define NO route handlers in this task. The router is created empty. L3-003, L3-004 and L3-006 each reopen this file in sequence - their depends_on entries chain them so they never write it concurrently.

Create file `app/main.py` containing a module-level FastAPI instance named `app`:
from fastapi import FastAPI from app.api import links
app = FastAPI(title="Link Shelf") app.include_router(links.router)
The instance must be named `app` at module level, because `app.main:app` is the import string a server would use and the smoke test imports that exact name.

`app/main.py` must import nothing from `app.db`, `app.models` or `app.schemas`. Its only project import is `from app.api import links`. This keeps the module importable in the declared layer order, where app/db.py and app/models/link.py do not yet exist.
Deviation from the layer plan, recorded rather than made silently: the plan's description for L3-002 says main.py should "import get_db and trigger schema creation". L4-001's own description places `Base.metadata.create_all` inside app/db.py, so importing get_db into main.py would be dead code that ALSO makes this task unbuildable in its declared position, for no gain. Written the buildable way deliberately.

Set the application title to exactly `Link Shelf` (matching the PRD's `meta`/`name` element). Do not set a version, description, or any other FastAPI constructor argument - none is specified anywhere in the PRD and inventing one adds a value nobody chose.

test-requirements.test:
Test-first. Write every test below into `tests/test_app_smoke.py` BEFORE creating app/main.py and app/api/links.py, run `pytest tests/test_app_smoke.py` and watch it fail on the missing import, then write the two modules until it passes. Runner: pytest.
This file uses `TestClient` constructed directly on the app - it must NOT use a `client` or `db_session` fixture. Those fixtures live in tests/conftest.py, created by L4-004 in a later layer; depending on them here would make this task unbuildable for no benefit, since an empty router needs no database.
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from app.main import app

Test: test_app_object_exists_and_is_named - Assert `app.title == "Link Shelf"` - This test cites no acceptance criterion; it asserts requirement 4. No criterion in this PRD describes the application object's metadata.

Test: test_app_serves_its_openapi_schema - Build `client = TestClient(app)` - `response = client.get("/openapi.json")` - Assert `response.status_code == 200` - Assert `response.json()["info"]["title"] == "Link Shelf"` - This is the smoke assertion: a 200 here proves the ASGI application constructed, the router was included without a routing conflict, and the app can serve a request. Cites no acceptance criterion - no criterion in this PRD describes the OpenAPI schema.

Test: test_links_router_is_included_and_empty - `from app.api.links import router` - `from fastapi import APIRouter` - Assert `isinstance(router, APIRouter)` - Assert `router.routes == []`, proving no handler was added in this task (requirement 1) - Assert `router.prefix == ""`, proving the no-prefix contract that L3-003, L3-004 and L3-006 are written against - Cites no acceptance criterion; it asserts requirements 1 and the router-prefix constraint, which are structural decisions rather than product behaviour.

verification.step: Run: `python -c "from app.main import app; print(app.title)"` - must print exactly `Link Shelf`
Run: `python -c "from app.api.links import router; print(len(router.routes))"` - must print exactly `0`
Run: `pytest tests/test_app_smoke.py -v` - all 3 test functions pass
Verify: `app/main.py` contains no occurrence of the string `app.db`, `app.models` or `app.schemas`

exports.interface:
# app/main.py from fastapi import FastAPI from app.api import links
app: FastAPI # title="Link Shelf"; the links router is already included
# Import path for a server or a TestClient: app.main:app # Imports nothing from app.db, app.models or app.schemas.

# app/api/links.py from fastapi import APIRouter
router: APIRouter # tags=["links"], NO prefix, no routes yet
# Contract for every task that adds a handler to this file: # the router has NO prefix, so each handler declares its FULL path. # # @router.post("/links") -> POST /links (L3-003) # @router.get("/links") -> GET /links (L3-004) # @router.post("/links/{link_id}/tags") -> POST /links/{id}/tags (L3-006) # # Adding a handler requires no change to app/main.py: the router object is already # included, so a route registered on it is served automatically.
